overview: Yuji’s controller swaps passive buffs as his cursed-energy level changes. His export leaves all unique slots empty.
technicalOverview: Yuji Itadori (CP_010) is a playable Jujutsu Sorcerer whose exported CharacterDataTable row has no unique-data rows at all: all nine Id_CharacterUnique entries are None and no CP_010 row exists in any of the five CharacterUniqueDataTable exports. Character setup still builds an all-null UniqueRows array, and the shared unique-float accessor is an unchecked row/value dereference, so there is no shipped CP_010 unique-float tuning to document. His behaviour comes from the ordinary action, command, special-attack and stat tables plus UCP_010_ActionController: that controller has no members and only swaps passive buffs when the cursed-energy level changes, while CreateAction is a plain pass-through to the shared action factory. UCP_010_BehaviorController is an equally small shell with a forward-only AI factory, and the CP_010 think node doubles as the game's default AI node. CP_010 is also the default character id used by many battle, free-battle, menu and save settings.

notes.text: No unique row exists for CP_010. The authoritative row input is empty: every one of the nine Id_CharacterUnique names in the exported CharacterDataTable row is None, and none of CharacterUniqueDataTable1..5 contains a CP_010 key. Character setup empties UniqueRows and adds one optional-table result per configured id, so all nine entries are null. AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue reads UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] with no bounds or null check, and FGameCharacterAction::GetOwnerUniqueFloat is just the qualified forward to it. There is therefore no CP_010-specific unique value to assign; any value seen in a modded or future row would be new data, not a shipped default.

The action controller is a memberless shell with exactly two late overrides. OnCursedEnergyLevelChanged calls the base first; the base sets the controller's cursed-energy level to min(NewLevel, 3) unless an attack action is active. CP_010 then removes every EGameBuffDebuff::CP_010_Passive stack at level 1, adds BUFF_CP_010_PASSIVE_2 at level 2, and adds BUFF_CP_010_PASSIVE_3 at both level 3 and level 4. CreateAction is only a Super forward, so CP_010 has no special action type of its own and uses the inherited 120-case action factory. Verification records CP_010 as the one 'verified-empty' shell whose late-slot overrides were already complete.

The level-swapped passives do have traced gameplay effects, but through BuffDebuffDataTable, not the unique table. The exported BUFF_CP_010_PASSIVE_2 and BUFF_CP_010_PASSIVE_3 rows are both EGameBuffDebuff::CP_010_Passive with FloatValue[0] = 0.9 / 0.8 and FloatValue[1] = 1.1 / 1.2. The status controller treats that buff type as a buff, adds its FloatValue[0] to the dash gauge consume-rate accumulator, and adds FloatValue[1] to the dash-end, dash-begin, dash-air-begin and dash-air-end rigidity rates (base rate + buff value - 1). Both buff names are also in the full round-keep list. These are buff-row floats, so they must not be entered into a CharacterUniqueDataTable row.

The behaviour controller is a size-0x50 memberless shell: its constructor adds no tables or fields, and slot-87 CreateThinkParam simply returns the parent's result. Verification found that CN_071 and CN_170 pass the identical ClassConstructor as CP_010, so they install CP_010's vtable and inherit that pure-forward slot-87 rather than having their own factory. That is a shared shell/vtable quirk, not evidence that those characters use CP_010's actions or tuning.

CP_010 has AIType 1 and its own FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CP_010. The AI brain also selects this node as the default for None/out-of-range AI types, and CN_170's type-29 slot has no case, so it shares the CP_010 factory. CP_010's think setup disables advanced AI behaviour, uses 800-unit close/mid ranges and 0.5-second think intervals, gives Cursed Energy Attack 1, Cursed Energy Attack 2 and Super Cursed Energy Attack weights 20, 20 and 30, gates CE2 on value D >= 4 and Super on MinAILevel, and limits Super to a 300-unit target range; random setup adds jump-air parameters 11-16 and step parameters 17 and 19, with 19 gated on value D >= 4. The reconstruction notes that SetupThinkParameters is still a DIFF row because of a callee mismatch, so these AI details are observed reconstruction rather than a byte-matched claim.

Shared systems can still ask any character for unique row 0, even when that character has no configured row. The AI curse-attack hold actions read (0,0) plus (1,0) or (2,0) when resetting their hold durations; ProjectionSorceryReceive uses (0,0) as restraint time only when the incoming request has no DamageTableRow; and SteerTowardSecondaryTarget reads (0,0) as an angle divisor, writing a zero turn time when it is not positive. Traps use FGameTrapAction::GetUniqueFloat to forward a value to their spawning character and return 0 if there is no source. CP_010's own CreateAction is a pass-through, and the reconstructed source does not show which of these generic paths CP_010 actually reaches with an all-null UniqueRows array; whether any of them would be exercised is unresolved, and the accessor itself has no null guard.

No unique camera preset is configured for CP_010. The shared MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads up to eleven floats from one unique row only when CameraMode is 2: indices 0-2 make the camera offset, 3-4 the up/down angle limits, 5-6 the field of view and blend time, 7 selects the FOV easing among four cases, and 8-10 set orbit yaw, pitch and roll. CP_010 has neither a unique row to supply these values nor a camera-specific override in its action controller; the helper is generic and must not be attributed to another character's row in this wiki entry.

CP_010 is the game's fallback character id. The battle settings constructor sets CharacterId to CP_010 with variation, material pattern and pose 0, and the comment records that unversioned cooked data omits an id equal to CP_010, making the default load-bearing. GameManager and menu-sequence selection fall back to CP_010 when an id is None or unusable, free-battle character slots default to it, and the exported CharacterDataTable row lists 30 CP_010 variations. This default role is separate from the unique-row question: it concerns which character is selected, not any unique tuning row.
